props.title: The size follows the number on the cake.
props.lede: A 30th and a 50th are different parties, and the band that suits one is the wrong size for the other.

rows.term: The 30th: a trio, and the DJ after it
rows.text: The one that runs latest. A trio of guitar, bass and drums fills a floor without a stage, and the DJ takes the same sound system when the band is done. The funk band is the trio for a crowd that wants a groove.

rows.term: The 40th: a band that plays both halves
rows.text: A seated dinner and then the floor once somebody moves the furniture. Tejas Singh and Tony Medina both start small and finish as a four piece on one contract, and the soul and R&B band is the quartet for a crowd that grew up on those records.

rows.term: The 50th: a jazz duo under the dinner and the toasts
rows.text: More often a seated dinner with a toast in it than a floor. Upright bass and guitar, quiet under the conversation, silent for the toasts and back the moment the glass goes down. The jazz trio with brushed drums is the same booking for a bigger crowd.

rows.term: The 60th and past it: one musician, or two
rows.text: Earlier, warmer, more family and more of it sitting down. A solo guitarist, a pianist or the duo holds the evening from arrival through dessert, and a Spanish guitarist under a long family dinner is the request that comes up most.

props.html: The cost guide sets out what each size costs in Colorado.

props.title: The surprise, the toast, and the set built for one person.

rows.text: The guest of honor thinks it’s dinner with three friends, the private dining space is full of everyone they’ve known since school, and the band is already playing, so the first thing they hear as the door opens is their song. It runs on the same cue as a surprise proposal song.
Somebody stands up with a glass, and the music stops before they reach the microphone. When the toasts are a program, three speakers and a slideshow, we plan them with you on the run of show.

rows.term: The set built for the person
rows.text: Tell us the name, the number and a few of the songs, and the set is built from the years the guest of honor cares about: the college years for a 40th, the wedding years for a 60th. The whole song list is on the repertoire page.
Some 50ths sit down and some don’t, and a band that plays dinner quietly and then turns up covers both. The yacht rock band and the soul and R&B band both do that on one contract.

rows.text: The band plays the hits and hands the microphone to the friends who have been threatening to sing all night. Live band karaoke fits a club or a big main floor.

rows.term: The one song, learned for the night
rows.text: A singer and guitarist learns the song the guest of honor has loved for thirty years and plays it once, at the moment you choose.

rows.term: A flamenco set piece under a long dinner
rows.text: A table of twelve and a guitar in the corner with real technique in it, with Dirty Flamenco stepping forward for one set piece.

rows.term: A sing-along the whole family can join
rows.text: A 70th or an 80th usually has four generations in it, and the Beatles are the songbook all four know. Your Bird Can Sing gets the whole family singing.

items.q: Can we hire a band for a birthday party?
items.a: Yes, and the size follows the number on the cake: a trio or a quartet for a 30th or a 40th that ends on a dance floor, a jazz duo for a 50th that's a dinner with a toast in it, and one musician or a duo from arrival through dessert for a 60th and past it. It's one contract with one personal contact, booked through Signet Artists in Denver.

items.q: What size band for a 40th birthday party?
items.a: A trio or a quartet. A trio plays the dinner quietly and fills the floor afterward without a stage, and a quartet is the size for a club or a venue past a hundred guests. The DJ can carry the late end through the same sound system.

items.q: How do you handle a surprise birthday party?
items.a: The musicians are set up early and playing quietly, so the place looks like it simply has live music that night, and the guest of honor's song starts on a cue you and the band agree beforehand: a nod from the host or a text from the door.

items.q: Can the band learn the birthday person's favorite songs?
items.a: Yes. One learned song comes with every booking, and each one after it is its own line on the quote.

items.q: Can a band play a birthday party at home?
items.a: Yes. A solo musician takes about 6 by 4 feet on one dedicated circuit, a duo 8 by 6 and a trio 12 by 8, in the corner the party naturally faces, and every size plays dinner at a level the table talks across. Outdoors it plays on a covered, level and dry spot with power run to it, and whatever limit the HOA or the neighborhood puts on evening sound goes into the contract. An announcement microphone for the toasts comes with every size.
